location: No breaking step found. I checked every line of (i) and Steps 1–6 of (ii).
objection:
I found no error.

(i) The proof writes Q(x) as a sum over d ≤ √x of μ(d)⌊x/d²⌋. Replacing each floor by x/d² costs at most 1 per term, so at most √x in total. Completing the sum over d costs at most 2√x, using (0): with N = ⌊z⌋, the tail Σ_{d≥N+1} d^{-2} is at most 1/N, which is at most 2/z for z ≥ 1. This gives |Q(x) − 6x/π²| ≤ 3√x.

(ii)
- Step 1 uses only the fact (P1 (i)) that g(q,·) depends on l mod q.
- Step 2 quotes P1 (iii) exactly as stated. It uses only the case of squarefree n, which is the only case it needs. Also c_q ≤ (6/π²)ζ(2) = 1, and the product over p | (n, q₁) correctly expands as Σ_{r|(n,q₁)} μ(r)/r.
- Step 3: for squarefree r, rm is squarefree exactly when m is squarefree and (m, r) = 1. The double Möbius expansion is effectively a finite sum. A pair with d ≤ √y but [d², e] > y has floor 0, so replacing it costs less than 1. The tail is bounded through [d², e] ≥ d². The case y < 1 is handled using |κ_r| ≤ 2·2^{ω(r)}.
- Step 4: all terms are nonnegative, so extending the sum to all squarefree r is legitimate. The Euler product is ∏(1 + 2p^{-3/2}) ≤ e^{2ζ(3/2)}, an absolute constant.
- Step 5: q is fixed and there are only finitely many residues l, so the limit S(x)/x → Σ g² is justified. Hence M_q = Σ_l g(q,l)².

The resulting bound 3B√x/q holds for every x > 0 and every q ≥ 1, with B absolute. So the claim holds as stated, with the same ranges and an absolute constant c₀.

The proof cites no external literature, so the 2010 cutoff does not arise. It uses P1 only as stated in deps/P1.md.

Numerical check: I computed Σ_l g(q,l)E(x;q,l) directly, taking g from the P1 (i) series. I used q ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 30, 36, 210, 1000, 2310} and x ∈ {10, 10³, 5·10⁴, 2·10⁵}. The largest value of |Σ g E|·q/√x was about 0.27. This is consistent with the claim and far below 3e^{2ζ(3/2)} ≈ 558.
other_issues: Wording only: the sentence "Every squarefree-indicator identity gives Q(x)=…" in part (i) is garbled; it presumably means "The identity μ²(n)=Σ_{d²|n}μ(d) gives". This does not affect correctness.
The constant c₀ = 3e^{2ζ(3/2)} ≈ 558 is very generous. That is acceptable, because the statement only asks for some absolute constant.
